questions.question:
A survey was conducted by a group of students as a part of their environment awareness programme, in which they collected the following data regarding the number of plants in 20 houses in a locality. (number of plants : number of houses)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 2 & 1 \\ \hline 2 - 4 & 2 \\ \hline 4 - 6 & 1 \\ \hline 6 - 8 & 5 \\ \hline 8 - 10 & 6 \\ \hline 10 - 12 & 2 \\ \hline 12 - 14 & 3 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mean number of plants per house. Which method did you use for finding the mean, and why?
answer_steps: The numbers are small, so the direct method is the easiest.

questions.question:
Consider the following distribution of daily wages (in ₹) of 50 workers of a factory. (daily wages in ₹ : number of workers)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 500 - 520 & 12 \\ \hline 520 - 540 & 14 \\ \hline 540 - 560 & 8 \\ \hline 560 - 580 & 6 \\ \hline 580 - 600 & 10 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mean daily wages of the workers of the factory by using an appropriate method.

The following distribution shows the daily pocket allowance of children of a locality. The mean pocket allowance is ₹ 18. Find the missing frequency $f$. (daily pocket allowance in ₹ : number of children)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 11 - 13 & 7 \\ \hline 13 - 15 & 6 \\ \hline 15 - 17 & 9 \\ \hline 17 - 19 & 13 \\ \hline 19 - 21 & f \\ \hline 21 - 23 & 5 \\ \hline 23 - 25 & 4 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Thirty women were examined in a hospital by a doctor and the number of heartbeats per minute were recorded and summarised as follows. (number of heartbeats per minute : number of women)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 65 - 68 & 2 \\ \hline 68 - 71 & 4 \\ \hline 71 - 74 & 3 \\ \hline 74 - 77 & 8 \\ \hline 77 - 80 & 7 \\ \hline 80 - 83 & 4 \\ \hline 83 - 86 & 2 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mean heartbeats per minute for these women, choosing a suitable method.

In a retail market, fruit vendors were selling mangoes kept in packing boxes. These boxes contained varying number of mangoes. The following was the distribution of mangoes according to the number of boxes. (number of mangoes : number of boxes)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 50 - 52 & 15 \\ \hline 53 - 55 & 110 \\ \hline 56 - 58 & 135 \\ \hline 59 - 61 & 115 \\ \hline 62 - 64 & 25 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mean number of mangoes kept in a packing box. Which method of finding the mean did you choose?
answer_steps: The classes are not continuous, but the class marks are the same: $x_i = 51, 54, 57, 60, 63$

questions.question:
The table below shows the daily expenditure on food of 25 households in a locality. (daily expenditure in ₹ : number of households)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 100 - 150 & 4 \\ \hline 150 - 200 & 5 \\ \hline 200 - 250 & 12 \\ \hline 250 - 300 & 2 \\ \hline 300 - 350 & 2 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mean daily expenditure on food by a suitable method.

To find out the concentration of SO₂ in the air (in parts per million, i.e., ppm), the data was collected for 30 localities in a certain city and is presented below. (concentration of SO₂ in ppm : frequency)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0.00 - 0.04 & 4 \\ \hline 0.04 - 0.08 & 9 \\ \hline 0.08 - 0.12 & 9 \\ \hline 0.12 - 0.16 & 2 \\ \hline 0.16 - 0.20 & 4 \\ \hline 0.20 - 0.24 & 2 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mean concentration of SO₂ in the air.

A class teacher has the following absentee record of 40 students of a class for the whole term. (number of days : number of students)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 6 & 11 \\ \hline 6 - 10 & 10 \\ \hline 10 - 14 & 7 \\ \hline 14 - 20 & 4 \\ \hline 20 - 28 & 4 \\ \hline 28 - 38 & 3 \\ \hline 38 - 40 & 1 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mean number of days a student was absent.

The following table gives the literacy rate (in percentage) of 35 cities. (literacy rate in % : number of cities)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 45 - 55 & 3 \\ \hline 55 - 65 & 10 \\ \hline 65 - 75 & 11 \\ \hline 75 - 85 & 8 \\ \hline 85 - 95 & 3 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mean literacy rate.

The following table shows the ages of the patients admitted in a hospital during a year. (age in years : number of patients)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 5 - 15 & 6 \\ \hline 15 - 25 & 11 \\ \hline 25 - 35 & 21 \\ \hline 35 - 45 & 23 \\ \hline 45 - 55 & 14 \\ \hline 55 - 65 & 5 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mode and the mean of the data given above. Compare and interpret the two measures of central tendency.
answer_steps: Mode $= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 35 + \dfrac{2}{11} \times 10$
The most common age is about 36.8 years, while the average age is about 35.37 years.

questions.question:
The following data gives the information on the observed lifetimes (in hours) of 225 electrical components. (lifetime in hours : frequency)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 20 & 10 \\ \hline 20 - 40 & 35 \\ \hline 40 - 60 & 52 \\ \hline 60 - 80 & 61 \\ \hline 80 - 100 & 38 \\ \hline 100 - 120 & 29 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Determine the modal lifetimes of the components.
answer_steps: Mode $= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 60 + \dfrac{9}{32} \times 20$

questions.question:
The following data gives the distribution of total monthly household expenditure of 200 families of a village. (expenditure in ₹ : number of families)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 1000 - 1500 & 24 \\ \hline 1500 - 2000 & 40 \\ \hline 2000 - 2500 & 33 \\ \hline 2500 - 3000 & 28 \\ \hline 3000 - 3500 & 30 \\ \hline 3500 - 4000 & 22 \\ \hline 4000 - 4500 & 16 \\ \hline 4500 - 5000 & 7 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the modal monthly expenditure of the families. Also, find the mean monthly expenditure.
answer_steps: Mode $= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 1500 + \dfrac{16}{23} \times 500$

questions.question:
The following distribution gives the state-wise teacher-student ratio in higher secondary schools of India. (number of students per teacher : number of states / U.T.)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 15 - 20 & 3 \\ \hline 20 - 25 & 8 \\ \hline 25 - 30 & 9 \\ \hline 30 - 35 & 10 \\ \hline 35 - 40 & 3 \\ \hline 40 - 45 & 0 \\ \hline 45 - 50 & 0 \\ \hline 50 - 55 & 2 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mode and mean of this data. Interpret the two measures.
answer_steps: Mode $= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 30 + \dfrac{1}{8} \times 5$
Most states have about 30.6 students per teacher; the average is about 29.2.

questions.question:
The given distribution shows the number of runs scored by some top batsmen of the world in one-day international cricket matches. (runs scored : number of batsmen)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 3000 - 4000 & 4 \\ \hline 4000 - 5000 & 18 \\ \hline 5000 - 6000 & 9 \\ \hline 6000 - 7000 & 7 \\ \hline 7000 - 8000 & 6 \\ \hline 8000 - 9000 & 3 \\ \hline 9000 - 10000 & 1 \\ \hline 10000 - 11000 & 1 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mode of the data.
answer_steps: Mode $= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 4000 + \dfrac{14}{23} \times 1000$

questions.question:
A student noted the number of cars passing through a spot on a road for 100 periods each of 3 minutes and summarised it in the table given below. (number of cars : frequency)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 10 & 7 \\ \hline 10 - 20 & 14 \\ \hline 20 - 30 & 13 \\ \hline 30 - 40 & 12 \\ \hline 40 - 50 & 20 \\ \hline 50 - 60 & 11 \\ \hline 60 - 70 & 15 \\ \hline 70 - 80 & 8 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mode of the data.
answer_steps: Mode $= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 40 + \dfrac{8}{17} \times 10$

questions.question:
The following frequency distribution gives the monthly consumption of electricity of 68 consumers of a locality. (monthly consumption in units : number of consumers)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 65 - 85 & 4 \\ \hline 85 - 105 & 5 \\ \hline 105 - 125 & 13 \\ \hline 125 - 145 & 20 \\ \hline 145 - 165 & 14 \\ \hline 165 - 185 & 8 \\ \hline 185 - 205 & 4 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the median, mean and mode of the data and compare them.
answer_steps: All three are close to each other, about 136 to 137 units.

questions.question:
If the median of the distribution given below is 28.5, find the values of $x$ and $y$. The total frequency is 60. (class interval : frequency)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 10 & 5 \\ \hline 10 - 20 & x \\ \hline 20 - 30 & 20 \\ \hline 30 - 40 & 15 \\ \hline 40 - 50 & y \\ \hline 50 - 60 & 5 \\ \hline\end{array}$$
answer_steps: The median $28.5$ lies in $20 - 30$, with $cf = 5 + x$, $f = 20$, $h = 10$.

questions.question:
A life insurance agent found the following data for the distribution of ages of 100 policy holders. Calculate the median age, if policies are given only to persons having age 18 years onwards but less than 60 years. (age below : number of policy holders)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 20 & 2 \\ \hline 25 & 6 \\ \hline 30 & 24 \\ \hline 35 & 45 \\ \hline 40 & 78 \\ \hline 45 & 89 \\ \hline 50 & 92 \\ \hline 55 & 98 \\ \hline 60 & 100 \\ \hline\end{array}$$
answer_steps: The cumulative frequencies are given: $\dfrac{n}{2} = 50$, and the first $cf \geq 50$ is $78$, for the class $35 - 40$.

questions.question:
The lengths of 40 leaves of a plant are measured correct to the nearest millimetre, and the data obtained is represented in the following table. (length in mm : number of leaves)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 118 - 126 & 3 \\ \hline 127 - 135 & 5 \\ \hline 136 - 144 & 9 \\ \hline 145 - 153 & 12 \\ \hline 154 - 162 & 5 \\ \hline 163 - 171 & 4 \\ \hline 172 - 180 & 2 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the median length of the leaves.
answer_steps: Make the classes continuous: $117.5 - 126.5$, $126.5 - 135.5$, and so on.

questions.question:
The following table gives the distribution of the life time of 400 neon lamps. (life time in hours : number of lamps)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 1500 - 2000 & 14 \\ \hline 2000 - 2500 & 56 \\ \hline 2500 - 3000 & 60 \\ \hline 3000 - 3500 & 86 \\ \hline 3500 - 4000 & 74 \\ \hline 4000 - 4500 & 62 \\ \hline 4500 - 5000 & 48 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the median life time of a lamp.

100 surnames were randomly picked up from a local telephone directory and the frequency distribution of the number of letters in the English alphabets in the surnames was obtained as follows. (number of letters : number of surnames)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 1 - 4 & 6 \\ \hline 4 - 7 & 30 \\ \hline 7 - 10 & 40 \\ \hline 10 - 13 & 16 \\ \hline 13 - 16 & 4 \\ \hline 16 - 19 & 4 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Determine the median number of letters in the surnames. Find the mean number of letters in the surnames. Also, find the modal size of the surnames.

The distribution below gives the weights of 30 students of a class. (weight in kg : number of students)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 40 - 45 & 2 \\ \hline 45 - 50 & 3 \\ \hline 50 - 55 & 8 \\ \hline 55 - 60 & 6 \\ \hline 60 - 65 & 6 \\ \hline 65 - 70 & 3 \\ \hline 70 - 75 & 2 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the median weight of the students.

questions.question: The median of a set of 9 distinct observations is 20.5. If each of the observations of the set is increased by 2, then the median of the new set
options: is increased by 2
is decreased by 2
is two times the original number
remains the same as that of the original observations
questions.explanation: Adding 2 to every observation moves the middle one up by 2 as well: the new median is 22.5.
option_feedback: Correct!
Every value goes up, so the middle value goes up.
Adding 2 does not double anything.
The middle observation itself increases by 2.

questions.question:
If the mode of the following distribution is 55, then find the value of $x$. Hence, find the mean. (class interval : frequency)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 15 & 10 \\ \hline 15 - 30 & 7 \\ \hline 30 - 45 & x \\ \hline 45 - 60 & 15 \\ \hline 60 - 75 & 10 \\ \hline 75 - 90 & 12 \\ \hline\end{array}$$
answer_steps: The mode 55 lies in the modal class $45 - 60$: $l = 45$, $h = 15$, $f_1 = 15$, $f_0 = x$, $f_2 = 10$.

questions.question:
A survey regarding heights (in cm) of 51 girls of class X of a school was conducted and the following data was obtained. Find the median height of girls. If mode of the above distribution is 148.05, find the mean using empirical formula. (height less than, in cm : number of girls)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 140 & 4 \\ \hline 145 & 11 \\ \hline 150 & 29 \\ \hline 155 & 40 \\ \hline 160 & 46 \\ \hline 165 & 51 \\ \hline\end{array}$$
The class mark of the class $10 - 25$ is:
option_feedback: That is the lower limit.
That is the sum; halve it.
Correct!
That is the class size.

questions.question: In the step-deviation method, $u_i$ is:
options: $\dfrac{a - x_i}{h}$
$\dfrac{x_i - a}{h}$
$x_i - a$
$\dfrac{x_i}{h}$
questions.explanation: Deviation from the assumed mean $a$, divided by the class size $h$.
option_feedback: The order is $x_i - a$.
Correct!
That is $d_i$; divide by $h$.
Subtract the assumed mean first.

questions.question: The modal class of a grouped frequency distribution is the class with the:
options: highest frequency
highest class mark
highest cumulative frequency
middle position
questions.explanation: Mode means the most frequent, so the modal class has the highest frequency.
option_feedback: Correct!
Mode is about how often, not how big.
That is always the last class.
That is the idea of the median.

questions.question: To find the median of grouped data, we first need the:
options: class marks
modal class
assumed mean
cumulative frequencies
questions.explanation: The median class is found from the cumulative frequencies.
option_feedback: Class marks are for the mean.
The modal class is for the mode.
The assumed mean is for the mean.
Correct!

questions.question: The empirical relation between mean, median and mode is:
options: $3 \times$ Mode $=$ Median $+ 2 \times$ Mean
Mode $=$ Mean $+$ Median
$3 \times$ Median $=$ Mode $+ 2 \times$ Mean
$3 \times$ Mean $=$ Mode $+ 2 \times$ Median
option_feedback: It is 3 times the median.
Mode $= 3 \times$ Median $- 2 \times$ Mean.
Correct!
Median and mean are swapped.

questions.question: If the mean of a distribution is 20 and its median is 22, then its mode (by the empirical relation) is:
option_feedback: Mode $= 3 \times 22 - 2 \times 20$.
Correct!
That is the average of 20 and 22.

questions.question: For a grouped distribution, $\sum f_i x_i = 1500$ and $\sum f_i = 50$. The mean is:
option_feedback: Correct!
Divide 1500 by 50, not 20.
Divide, do not subtract.

questions.question: In the median formula $l + \dfrac{\frac{n}{2} - cf}{f} \times h$, $cf$ is the cumulative frequency of:
options: the median class
the last class
the class after the median class
the class before the median class
questions.explanation: It is the running total up to the class just before the median class.
option_feedback: Use the running total before the median class.
That is the total $n$.
Use the class before it.
Correct!

questions.question: In the mode formula, $f_2$ is the frequency of:
options: the modal class
the last class
the class after the modal class
the class before the modal class
questions.explanation: $f_0$ is before, $f_1$ is the modal class, $f_2$ is after.
option_feedback: That is $f_1$.
$f_2$ is the modal class's next neighbour.
Correct!
That is $f_0$.

questions.question: The classes 118–126, 127–135, … are made continuous by changing the first class to:
questions.explanation: The gap between 126 and 127 is 1, so subtract 0.5 from each lower limit and add 0.5 to each upper limit.
option_feedback: Subtract 0.5, not 1.
The lower limit goes down to 117.5.
Correct!
Move both limits by 0.5.

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

R does explain A: this formula is exactly what gives 17.5.

**Assertion (A):** For the classes 118–126, 127–135, …, the lower limit of the class 127–135 used in the median formula is 127.

**Reason (R):** The median formula needs continuous classes.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Check the Assertion again: it is false, because the continuous class is 126.5–135.5, so the lower limit is 126.5.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** The assumed mean method gives the same mean as the direct method.

**Reason (R):** The assumed mean must be one of the class marks.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Check the Reason again: it is false, because any number can be the assumed mean.
Correct! A is true: the assumed mean only shifts the numbers and shifts them back. R is false: any number can be the assumed mean.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because the assumed mean only shifts the numbers and shifts them back.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** The median of the observations 1, 3, 5, 7 is 5.

**Reason (R):** For an even number of observations, the median is the mean of the two middle observations.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.question: Find the class marks of the classes $10 - 25$ and $35 - 55$.
If the mode of a distribution is 24.5 and its mean is 29.75, find its median using the empirical relation.

Find the mode of the following distribution. (class interval : frequency)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 10 & 5 \\ \hline 10 - 20 & 8 \\ \hline 20 - 30 & 7 \\ \hline 30 - 40 & 12 \\ \hline 40 - 50 & 28 \\ \hline 50 - 60 & 20 \\ \hline 60 - 70 & 10 \\ \hline 70 - 80 & 10 \\ \hline\end{array}$$
answer_steps: Mode $= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 40 + \dfrac{16}{24} \times 10$

questions.question:
Find the median of the following distribution. (class interval : frequency)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 10 & 8 \\ \hline 10 - 20 & 16 \\ \hline 20 - 30 & 36 \\ \hline 30 - 40 & 34 \\ \hline 40 - 50 & 6 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Find the mean of the following distribution by the step-deviation method. (class interval : frequency)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 20 & 6 \\ \hline 20 - 40 & 8 \\ \hline 40 - 60 & 10 \\ \hline 60 - 80 & 12 \\ \hline 80 - 100 & 6 \\ \hline 100 - 120 & 5 \\ \hline 120 - 140 & 3 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

The median of the following data is 525. Find the values of $x$ and $y$, if the total frequency is 100. (class interval : frequency)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 100 & 2 \\ \hline 100 - 200 & 5 \\ \hline 200 - 300 & x \\ \hline 300 - 400 & 12 \\ \hline 400 - 500 & 17 \\ \hline 500 - 600 & 20 \\ \hline 600 - 700 & y \\ \hline 700 - 800 & 9 \\ \hline 800 - 900 & 7 \\ \hline 900 - 1000 & 4 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

questions.question:
A school surveyed the daily screen time (in hours) of 50 students. (screen time in hours : number of students)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline 0 - 2 & 8 \\ \hline 2 - 4 & 14 \\ \hline 4 - 6 & 16 \\ \hline 6 - 8 & 8 \\ \hline 8 - 10 & 4 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

(i) Write the modal class. (1)

(ii) Write the median class. (1)

(iii) Find the mode. OR Find the mean screen time. (2)
answer_steps: (ii) $\dfrac{n}{2} = 25$; cumulative frequencies $8, 22, 38$: the median class is $4 - 6$
